edition.name: Migne, Patrologia Latina (PL 2, Paris 1844), De praescriptionibus adversus haereticos, via Latin Wikisource transcription
edition.witness_note: Single locked witness in repo; second witness not yet locked.

source_text: Sed ipsi de Scripturis agunt, et de Scripturis suadent. Aliunde scilicet loqui possent de rebus fidei, nisi ex literis fidei? Venimus igitur ad propositum: huc enim dirigebamus, et hoc praestruebamus allocutionis praefatione, ut jam hinc de eo congrediamur, de quo adversarii provocant. Scripturas obtendunt, et hac sua audacia statim quosdam movent; in ipso vero congressu firmos quidem fatigant, infirmos capiunt, medios cum scrupulo dimittunt. Hunc igitur potissimum gradum obstruimus, non admittendos eos ad ullam de Scripturis disputationem. Si hae sunt illae vires eorum, uti eas habere possint, dispici debet cui competat possessio Scripturarum, ne is admittatur ad eas, cui nullo modo competit.
pass_a_gloss: But they themselves deal with the Scriptures, and persuade from the Scriptures. For evidently they could not speak about the matters of faith from anywhere else, if not from the letters of faith. We come therefore to the proposed thing: for we were directing it here, and we were preparing this with the preface of the speech, so that we may now clash with this, about which our adversaries provoke. They display the Scriptures, and with this their audacity they immediately move certain ones; but in the actual clash they indeed weary the strong, capture the weak, and send away those in the middle with a scruple. Therefore we block this step especially, not allowing them to be admitted to any discussion about the Scriptures. If these are those strengths of theirs, so that they may be able to have them, it ought to be examined to whom the possession of the Scriptures belongs, lest he be admitted to them, to whom it does not belong in any way.

choices.english: to whom the possession of the Scriptures belongs
rejected: who has the right to interpret Scripture

pass_b_english: But they themselves traffic in the Scriptures and argue from them; obviously they could not speak about the faith from any other source than the letters of faith. So we arrive at the point we aimed for: we steered the discussion here and prefaced our address precisely so that we can now engage the very issue our opponents raise. They flaunt the Scriptures, and their sheer audacity instantly sways some people; yet in the actual confrontation they merely exhaust the strong, ensnare the weak, and dismiss the undecided with a lingering doubt. Consequently we bar this move outright, refusing them any place in a scriptural debate. If these are indeed their strong points, enabling them to claim them, then it must be determined who rightfully possesses the Scriptures, lest anyone who has no claim whatsoever be admitted to them.

anf_compare.notes: Drafted from source only; ANF not shown to drafter.

review.notes: The translation accurately reflects the Latin text. Pass A and Pass B maintain the nuances of the original, such as the distinction between the strong, weak, and middle (medios) and the conditional nature of the final sentence. The title 'Authority of Scripture' correctly names the thought of the passage regarding the right to possess and use the Scriptures.
